description.narrative: Denna isats rör projektstöd till Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC), specifikt avdelningen med namnet Women and Youth Peace and Security Institute, WYPSI. Det övergripande syftet är att stärka kvinnor och ungas bidrag till arbetet för hållbar fred och säkerhet i Afrika. Insatsen följer tidigare projektstöd under perioden 2019-2023. Programmet sköts ifrån KAIPTCs kontor i Accra, Ghana.

This contribution concerns support to the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC), more specifically support to the Women and Youth Peace and Security Institute (WYPSI). The overall goal of the project is "To enhance the role of women and youth to contribute to achieving sustainable peace and security in Africa". The planned contribution follows previous support to the programme "Enhancing the Operationalization of the Women, Peace and Security Agenda in Africa", with a budget of 15 MSEK over three years (2019­2023). As for the previous support, KAIPTC will be the direct and only recipient of the funding for this planned contribution and the programme will be managed from its office based in Accra, Ghana.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The first reporting for the project, covering the period 1 October 2023 - 31 December 2024 (Year 1) was due in March 2025 and received with some delays (see statement on report).
Examples of key results, from the narrative report:
- The theoretical knowledge of grassroots women in Ghana was significantly enhanced to expedite the implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) agenda at the community level. Targeted trainees empowered women to actively participate in peacebuilding and advocacy efforts. This initiative bolstered the capacity of grassroots women to become key drivers of the WPS agenda within their communities.
- Stakeholder consultative meetings in Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Senegal, and Ghana effectively identified challenges, opportunities, and actionable recommendations to progress Africas Youth, Peace, and Security (YPS) agenda. These engagements brought together a diverse range of stakeholders, fostering dialogue to tackle gaps such as limited youth inclusion, gender disparities, and insufficient institutional coordination. Key outcomes, including a validated roadmap and actionable recommendations, established a solid foundation for integrating YPS into education, utilising technology for peacebuilding, and enhancing interregional collaboration. Following up on this, the Symposium served as a platform for sharing best practices across the continent even beyond the physical engagement.
Results tend to be reported on activity/output level and it is difficult to follow or demonstrate any change beyond output level. Sida discussed with KAIPTC the possibility of including them in a training on RBM when/if such training takes place in 2025.
The final payment (5MSEK) was released in June 2025 to cover the 2025 year activities; this was delayed due to late submission and consequent review and approval of first reporting 2023/2024 and WP/budget 2025. The support will be ended in December 2025.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
